old_title: Celtic under pressure and eyeing revenge against bitter rivals Rangers in Old Firm
new_title: Rangers add to Celtic misery with deserved second Old Firm win in a week
old_text:
Celtic will be out for revenge as they host Rangers in the first Old Firm clash of the Scottish Premiership season.
The Gers powered to an impressive 3-0 victory over their rivals in the League Cup quarter-finals at Ibrox last weekend, a result that could give Derek McInnes lift off after a difficult start to life in Glasgow.
But with away fans banned from matches between the Old Firm teams in the Premiership and League Cup this season, it is Celtic and Martin O'Neill's side who will have home advantage at Parkhead this afternoon.
A deflating defeat to Ferencvaros in the Europa League in midweek means Celtic have lost back-to-back matches under O'Neill, but they have won six games from six to start their Premiership title defence. Can Rangers eat into their early five-point advantage or can Celtic stretch their lead at the top?
Follow live updates from Celtic v Rangers in the Old Firm, below
Celtic 0-0 Rangers, 2 mins
A couple of crunching 50-50s early on. You wouldn't expect anything less in the Old Firm.
And Rangers nearly score straight away! Raskin with a gorgeous ball in behind, Gassama with a yard of space but Donovan gets back brilliantly to put in the challenge and block it out for a goal-kick
KICK-OFF! Celtic v Rangers
Underway at a Celtic Park shorn of Rangers supporters. Can Celtic start better than they did a week ago?
Celtic v Rangers
Here's a reminder of the teams today.
In the game of Celtic goalkeeper flip-flop, Viljami Sinisalo gets the nod over Sam Johnstone this week, while Luke McCowan starts in attack. Haissem Hassan is still only on the bench for the Hoops. They go for three at the back after being surprised by Rangers doing that last weekend
Meanwhile, Rangers are unchanged from a week ago and that demolition of Celtic. Will James Penrice be in midfield again? Surely he will and Gers will persist with the three at the back that stunned their bitter rivals
Celtic XI: Sinisalo; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Trusty, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Baur; McCowan, Duran, Nygren.
Rangers XI: Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Neil; Gassama, Kim, Kelsy; Naderi
Ivor Pandur eyeing Old Firm repeat
Rangers goalkeeper Ivor Pandur got his first taste of Old Firm action last weekend, having signed from Hull City in the summer, and he is eager to repeat the 3-0 triumph.
"We are confident. I think we did a really good job last Sunday and we just want to repeat that," said Pandur.
"Obviously we had a week to prepare to see what we can improve on, do better. But the performance was good and we want to do the same.
"The experience was really good. Obviously, people can tell you but when you step on the pitch and you hear the sound and feel the energy, it's something different to what I have experienced in my life.
"So, I am truly grateful that I was able to experience that."
Crowd can give us the edge, says Cameron Carter-Vickers
Celtic Park will be entirely green and white today, with away fans banned for Old Firm games this season.
And Celtic defender Cameron Carter-Vickers believes that could makea. big difference this afternoon.
"We want to come out on Sunday, with the crowd behind us and everyone together and try to put a performance together that will get the result we want," said Carter-Vickers.
"Hopefully, it'll make a difference (the fans). As a Celtic player, that's what you want - 60,000 Celtic fans behind you and pushing the team on.
"If we can get that on Sunday, I think it'll create a good atmosphere for us to perform."
Scotland and Celtic great Danny McGrain diagnosed with Alzheimer's
Some sad news emerged earlier this week, with former Celtic and Scotland captain Danny McGrain announcing that he has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease.
His family chose to disclose the diagnosis publicly "so that Danny can continue to receive the love and support of the Celtic Family, just as he has given so freely and humbly to others throughout his life".
In a statement released by the club, his wife Laraine said: "Danny received this diagnosis some time ago, and as time has moved on, we felt it was right to be open and clear.
"Danny has always loved helping supporters - whether through hospital visits, assisting fans with charity events, or sending messages of support.
"As time has gone on, that has become more difficult for Danny, so we wanted to explain his situation with honesty, and with the care and respect the Celtic Family has always shown us."
Arrivals at Celtic Park
Here's both teams entering the building a little earlier ahead of this Old Firm clash
Rangers team news - unchanged from last week
If it ain't broke, don't fix it. After their 3-0 demolition of Celtic last week, Derek McInnes has opted for an unchanged starting XI.
All eyes will be on James Penrice again to see if he's at left-back again in a four-at-the-back or if he pushes up into midfield, leaving a back three.
Djeidi Gassama and Kevin Kelsy both impressed on the wings last week, and will try to do so again.
Rangers XI: Pandur; Sterling, Fernandez, Makhanya, Penrice; Raskin, Neil; Gassama, Kim, Kelsy; Naderi
Celtic team news
Here's the team news for today, starting with Celtic.
Not unsurprisingly, Martin O'Neill has opted for Viljami Sinisalo in goal after Sam Johnstone's very shaky display in the Old Firm last weeked.
Once again, Haissem Hassan is only on the bench but Luke McCowan gets the start rather than Sebastian Tounekti. I fear that still won't be the most popular with Celtic fans though...
Camilo Duran looks to be leading the line with record signing Kasper Hogh on the bench and 3/5 at the back appears to be the order of the day again
Celtic XI: Sinisalo; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Trusty, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Baur; McCowan, Duran, Nygren
new_text:
Celtic failed to get revenge over Rangers as they lost 1-0 in the first Old Firm clash of the Scottish Premiership season, for a second defeat at the hands of their bitter rivals in a week
The Gers powered to an impressive 3-0 victory in the League Cup quarter-finals at Ibrox last weekend, and followed that up with another dominant display, although the scoreline was closer this time around.
Ryan Naderi slammed home a rebound on 33 minutes for the decisive goal and completed a week that has surely given Derek McInnes lift-off after a difficult start to life in Glasgow.
Away fans are banned from matches between the Old Firm teams in the Premiership and League Cup this season, so Celtic Park was exclusively green and white but that didn't help Martin O'Neill's side, who also endured a deflating defeat to Ferencvaros in the Europa League in midweek and have now lost three on the spin with the clouds of crisis beginning to gather over Parkhead.
Relive all the action from Celtic v Rangers in the Old Firm, below
Celtic booed off as week of woe ends with Rangers delivering another Old Firm humiliation
Rangers racked up a second win over Celtic in eight days as boos rung around an all-green Parkhead following a 1-0 defeat by the Light Blues.
Celtic's 74-year-old boss Martin O'Neill went into the game under the spotlight after two successive losses, including a bruising 3-0 Scottish League Cup loss to Gers at Ibrox last Sunday.
To silence inside a stadium populated with home fans only, Gers striker Ryan Naderi opened the scoring in the 33rd minute and it was enough for another huge victory for Derek McInnes's men who will feel they should have added to that goal after the break.
It was a first Scottish Premiership defeat of the season for the home side, who are just two points ahead of their Old Firm rivals at the top of the table going into the international break with more pressure on O'Neill.
Read the full report from Celtic Park:
Rangers narrow the gap at top of the Premiership
Celtic's 100 per cent record in the Scottish Premiership this season comes to an end and Rangers are now just two points behind them
'It was men against boys'
The pundits have had their say after that Old Firm clash and it wasn't pretty for Celtic...
Celtic 0-1 Rangers
Celebratory scenes for the Light Blues at Parkhead but dismay for Celtic!
WATCH! Naderi's goal wins Old Firm
Here's the moment that decided this Old Firm clash. Ryan Naderi slamming a rebound home.
Rangers were full value for their victory but this was what ultimately made the difference
FULL-TIME! Celtic 0-1 Rangers
All over at Celtic Park! Rangers full value for their 1-0 win after Ryan Naderi's first-half goal. They've beaten Celtic twice in a week for back-to-back Old Firm wins.
Celtic still top of the Scottish Premiership but the gap is now down to just two points. All the momentum is with Derek McInnes' men now!
Celtic 0-1 Rangers, 90+2 mins
Rangers have the ball down in the Celtic corner. This is ideal for them.
It comes out but a couple of crunching tackles in midfield from Rangers. Full commitment! And then Baur fouls Devlin out wide, so Rangers can take it back into the corner.
Celtic 0-1 Rangers, 90 mins
Four minutes of added time. Can Rangers see this out?
Celtic 0-1 Rangers, 88 mins
Play stops for 30 seconds while Scales re-ties his laces after losing his boot and then he promptly gives the ball away once we resume. Good stuff...
Raskin then gets a late yellow card.
Couple of Rangers subs to try and see this out. Chukwuani and Devlin on for Neil and Kelsy.
Celtic with a last throw of the dice - Liam Scales off and young Chelsea loanee Shim Mheuka on.
Celtic 0-1 Rangers, 86 mins
Celtic are starting to (finally) ramp up the pressure here. The fans are starting to make more noise as well.
They're putting balls into the box and then win a corner. The big boys come up from the back...
Hassan with a good cross, Scales flicks on, only half-cleared and Forrest's strike deflected over the bar for another corner.
This time Kelsy heads away Tounekti's cross and Rangers relieve the pressure for now.
